title: Grateful Dead Live at Cameron Indoor Stadium, Duke U on 1982-04-02
lineage: Cassette Master (Nakamichi DR-1) -> Sound Devices 744T (24bit/44.1k) -> Adobe Audition v3.0 -> Samplitude Professional v11.2 -> FLAC/16
source: (FOB) Nakamichi 700 (With Bass EQ) -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/Maxell XLIIS/Dolby B)

ai_review.summary: Punchy audience recording captures a high‑energy 1982 show highlighted by a piano‑driven Other One, scorching Little Red Rooster, Candyman and an epic China > Rider stretch.
ai_review.review: The tape delivers a clear, punchy audience sound that faithfully records the band’s fire‑brand performance. Standout moments include Brent’s piano‑like work on The Other One, a smoking Little Red Rooster with Brent’s scat, fierce renditions of Candyman and China > Rider, plus a powerful Dark Star and Samson jam. While a few reviewers note an average first set and some weaker second‑set choices, the overall energy is high and the recording quality is solid.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviews (5/6) give 5‑star praise for both performance and sound, noting a clear, punchy audience recording and many standout songs; only two mixed/negative notes keep the rating just below perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Very fine, punchy audience tape; crisp enough to capture dynamics, no major drop‑outs or muddiness reported.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
poor_songs: Second‑set song selection overall deemed weak by one reviewer
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set considered average by some but builds into a strong second half; transitions like Drums>Space>Other One and Truckin' are highlighted, while the encore is brief but spry.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Noted for dancing more than usual, swapping sides with Phil, delivering soaring solos on Candyman and Looks Like Rain, and feeding off Brent’s piano energy during The Other One.
band_member_comments.Phil: Swapped to stage right, creating a new interplay that many reviewers felt added intensity; bass work contributes to the overall fire‑brand vibe.
band_member_comments.Bob: Brent Mydland’s piano‑driven approach on The Other One, scat vocals on Little Red Rooster, and vocal leads on Samson and Truckin' are praised; his keyboard tone described as jazzy and possibly from a Yamaha.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent’s keyboards likened to jazz piano, providing a strong harmonic foundation especially in The Other One and Dark Star sections.
band_member_comments.Drums: The Drums>Space segment is highlighted as a strong moment, with Bill Kreutzmann’s playing contributing to the ‘great spaces’ of ’82.
